LESSON: PRESSURE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.2: Pressure
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 25

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Pressure, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does density of fluid, acceleration due to gravity and depth below the free surface affect pressure in fluid?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Pressure together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: the learner develops speaking and listening skills as they discuss the applications

of atmospheric pressure and transmission of pressure in fluids.

• Digital Literacy: the learner acquires manipulation skills as they use digital media with assistive technology to

search for more information on the applications of atmospheric pressure and transmission of pressure in fluids.

Values

• Love: the learner practices the virtue of sharing as they use available resources and avoid inflicting pain on others

while carrying out activities to demonstrate the existence of atmospheric pressure in nature.

• Respect: the learner acquires skills in respecting diverse opinions as they discuss the transmission of pressure in fluids

Suggested learning resources;

Candles, water, tin can, Ping pong ball, syringe, balloon, bottles, vase. Screen readers, screen magnifiers, adapted

keyboards, print media in appropriate font and colour contrast, braille, learners print and braille course book.
